headline: 3,431 passengers affected as Biman and US-Bangla suspend flights to Saudi Arabia
summary: Flight disruptions follow projectile attacks on Saudi airports, including King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which have caused multiple deaths and injuries.
details: Biman Bangladesh Airlines and US-Bangla Airlines have suspended flights to Riyadh and Dammam following projectile attacks and airport closures in Saudi Arabia.
US-Bangla has cancelled its Dhaka-Riyadh services until October 21, while Biman has suspended several flights, including its Dhaka-Riyadh and Dhaka-Dammam services.
According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), 10 flights between Dhaka and Riyadh have been cancelled over the past three days, affecting 3,431 passengers.

The disruptions come amid successive attacks on Saudi airports. A strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on October 10 killed 13 people, including two Bangladeshis, and injured over 300 others.
A subsequent attack on Sunday killed a Pakistani resident and injured 11 others, according to Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation.
Biman's Dammam-bound flight BG349 was diverted to Doha on October 11 due to the temporary closure of King Fahd International Airport, before eventually reaching Dammam safely.
Affected passengers are advised to contact their airlines or travel agencies for information on rebooking and flight status.
caption:
Over 3,400 passengers stranded as attacks on Saudi airports force Bangladeshi airlines to suspend flights.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines and US-Bangla Airlines have suspended flights to Riyadh and Dammam following projectile attacks and airport closures in Saudi Arabia.

US-Bangla has cancelled its Dhaka-Riyadh services until October 21, while Biman has suspended several flights, including its Dhaka-Riyadh and Dhaka-Dammam services.

According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), 10 flights between Dhaka and Riyadh have been cancelled over the past three days, affecting 3,431 passengers.

The disruptions come amid successive attacks on Saudi airports. A strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on October 10 killed 13 people, including two Bangladeshis, and injured over 300 others.

A subsequent attack on Sunday killed a Pakistani resident and injured 11 others, according to Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation.

Biman's Dammam-bound flight BG349 was diverted to Doha on October 11 due to the temporary closure of King Fahd International Airport, before eventually reaching Dammam safely.

Affected passengers are advised to contact their airlines or travel agencies for information on rebooking and flight status.

headline_marked: Litton Das ton: [[Bangladesh set Afghanistan 479-run target]] in one-off Test
headline: Litton Das ton: Bangladesh set Afghanistan 479-run target in one-off Test
summary: A brilliant century by Litton Das and a half-century from Mehidy Hasan Miraz propel the Tigers to a commanding lead in Abu Dhabi.
details: Litton Das struck his seventh Test century, scoring 102 off 117 balls with 14 fours, as Bangladesh declared their second innings at 372 for seven.
The declaration sets Afghanistan the mammoth task of chasing 479 runs to win with two days remaining in the one-off Test in Abu Dhabi.
Litton and Mehidy Hasan Miraz shared an unbroken 149-run seventh-wicket partnership, transforming Bangladesh's position and tightening their grip on the match.
Mehidy provided steadfast support, reaching his 11th Test half-century with an unbeaten 51 off 96 deliveries at the time of the declaration.
Litton's innings was marked by resilience, surviving several dropped catches and a turned-down caught-behind appeal despite a thin deflection.
Earlier in the second innings, Najmul Hossain Shanto (82) and Mushfiqur Rahim (81) provided a strong platform after the top order had stumbled to 53 for three.
Afghanistan, who were bowled out for 240 in their first innings, now face a daunting target of 479 runs to win the match.
Bangladesh will now look to their bowlers to secure the victory after the dominant batting performance from Litton and Miraz.
caption:
479 runs to win! Litton Das's masterclass century puts Bangladesh in a commanding position against Afghanistan.

Litton Das struck his seventh Test century, scoring 102 off 117 balls with 14 fours, as Bangladesh declared their second innings at 372 for seven.

The declaration sets Afghanistan the mammoth task of chasing 479 runs to win with two days remaining in the one-off Test in Abu Dhabi.

Litton and Mehidy Hasan Miraz shared an unbroken 149-run seventh-wicket partnership, transforming Bangladesh's position and tightening their grip on the match.

Mehidy provided steadfast support, reaching his 11th Test half-century with an unbeaten 51 off 96 deliveries at the time of the declaration.

Litton's innings was marked by resilience, surviving several dropped catches and a turned-down caught-behind appeal despite a thin deflection.

Earlier in the second innings, Najmul Hossain Shanto (82) and Mushfiqur Rahim (81) provided a strong platform after the top order had stumbled to 53 for three.

Afghanistan, who were bowled out for 240 in their first innings, now face a daunting target of 479 runs to win the match.

Bangladesh will now look to their bowlers to secure the victory after the dominant batting performance from Litton and Miraz.
